subject: frontend-engineering
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Concept of the skill, Coverage, Method, Verification, Do NOT Use When) and the Understanding fields (raw vs semantic token layering, component contracts, theming, governance, migration).

cases.scenario: A component library hardcodes hex values and palette-named CSS variables (--blue-500, --gray-200) directly inside button, card, and chart components. The team now wants dark mode.
cases.context: There is no semantic layer; every component references raw palette names. Dark mode would require editing every component.
cases.question: How should the agent restructure the tokens?
expected_flags: Introduce a semantic token layer (surface, text, primary-action, danger) that points at raw palette tokens
Components consume only semantic tokens, never raw palette names
Dark mode becomes a re-mapping of what raw values the semantic tokens resolve to, not a component rewrite
Flags that leaked palette names are the reason theming requires touching every component
expected_fix_hints: Define semantic tokens for product meaning and repoint components at them
Provide a light and dark resolution of the raw layer behind the same semantic names
absent_signals: Do not add a second set of hardcoded dark hex values inside components
Do not keep palette names inside component code

cases.scenario: A Button component has grown to 23 variants (primary-large-rounded, secondary-small-ghost-danger, ...) added one-by-one as designers asked for new looks. New requests keep arriving.
cases.context: Many variants overlap visually and only a handful map to a real, distinct use case.
cases.question: How should the agent respond to the variant sprawl?
expected_flags: Variants must map to real use cases, not visual guesses
Collapse overlapping variants into orthogonal props (intent, size, shape) rather than enumerated combinations
Too many escape hatches make the system ungoverned, not flexible
Establish theming/density rules and governance before multiplying variants further
expected_fix_hints: Refactor enumerated variants into composable contract props
Define which combinations are sanctioned and which are forbidden
absent_signals: Do not keep adding one new variant per request
Do not approve variants justified only by 'a slightly different look'

cases.scenario: A shared Modal component is reused across the app, but each team adds its own focus-trap, escape-key handling, and aria attributes locally — inconsistently. Some instances are inaccessible.
cases.context: Accessibility is treated as a per-screen add-on rather than part of the component.
cases.question: How should the agent fix the Modal's design?
expected_flags: Accessibility behavior (focus trap, escape handling, aria, focus return) belongs in the component contract, shipped once
Declare the contract: purpose, props/slots, states, accessibility behavior, composition rules
Give the component clear ownership and an API boundary so teams stop re-implementing behavior
Mark per-screen accessibility overrides as forbidden local overrides
expected_fix_hints: Move focus management and aria into the Modal implementation behind its contract
Document expected use and anti-use in the component docs
absent_signals: Do not leave accessibility to each consuming screen
Do not allow each team to re-implement modal behavior locally

cases.scenario: An old design system has tokens like --color-accent that 400 files use. A new canonical token --color-primary-action should replace it, but a hard rename would break production screens overnight.
cases.context: The team wants to converge on canonical tokens without a risky big-bang change.
cases.question: How should the agent plan the token migration?
expected_flags: Provide a migration path: alias the deprecated token to the canonical one, deprecate rather than delete
Detect drift between code usage and the canonical taxonomy
Migrate usages incrementally, verifying real screens still build without one-off styling
Mark the deprecated token with a removal plan, not an immediate removal
expected_fix_hints: Add a deprecation alias and migrate call sites in waves
Track remaining deprecated-token usages until zero, then remove
absent_signals: Do not hard-rename the token in one sweep
Do not delete the deprecated token before usages are migrated

cases.scenario: To move fast, a team adds a `style` and `className` passthrough plus a `tokenOverride` prop to every system component so product squads can tweak anything inline.
cases.context: Within weeks, screens diverge: spacing, color, and state styling are re-decided locally despite the system existing.
cases.question: How should the agent evaluate the universal override props?
expected_flags: Unbounded overrides make the system decorative — every screen re-decides locally
Define forbidden local overrides; constraints are what make the system reusable
Allow only bounded, contract-sanctioned customization (declared props), not arbitrary passthrough
Flags the override props as ungoverned flexibility, not real flexibility
expected_fix_hints: Replace arbitrary style/token passthrough with declared contract props
Document which customizations are sanctioned and enforce the rest as forbidden
absent_signals: Do not keep universal inline override props
Do not treat unconstrained escape hatches as flexibility

cases.scenario: A PM asks the design-system-architecture owner to decide the dashboard's section order and responsive breakpoints, and to rewrite the empty-state copy for the reports page.
cases.context: The team conflates 'the design system' with all design and content decisions.
cases.question: How should the agent scope the request?
expected_flags: Section order and breakpoints for one page are out of scope — that is layout-composition
Empty-state copy is out of scope — that is microcopy
Offer the in-scope part: which semantic tokens and component contracts those screens should consume
Correctly redirects rather than answering out of lane
expected_fix_hints: Hand page layout to layout-composition and copy to microcopy
Provide the system vocabulary (tokens, components) the page should be built from
absent_signals: Do not design the page's specific layout
Do not write the empty-state copy

cases.scenario: An audit of a maturing component library finds charts hardcoding status colors, three near-duplicate Card components, and a token file that no longer matches the Figma source of truth.
cases.context: The team wants to know what is structurally wrong, not just cosmetically.
cases.question: What should the agent's audit conclude and prioritize?
expected_flags: Charts/status colors should consume semantic tokens, not hardcoded raw values
Consolidate the near-duplicate Card components behind one contract with real-use-case variants
Token drift between code and design intent should be detected and reconciled
Frame findings as token-taxonomy and contract gaps, not visual polish
expected_fix_hints: Repoint hardcoded chart colors at semantic status tokens
Reconcile the code token file against the design source of truth and add drift detection
absent_signals: Do not treat the duplicates as acceptable variety
Do not leave hardcoded raw values in chart components
